surfshark.name: Surfshark

surfshark.keyPlaceholder: Paste the private key, or the whole WireGuard config

guide.title: How to get the private key
guide.step2: Go to VPN → Manual setup → Desktop or mobile → WireGuard.
guide.step3: Choose “I don't have a key pair” and generate a new key pair.
guide.step4: Copy the private key and paste it here.
guide.step5: Optional: download a location's config with the key, for its Address line — or import that .conf here directly.
guide.noteLabels: Button names on the page may differ slightly; follow the instructions there.

surfshark.addressHint: The Address line of the config Surfshark gave you with this key, e.g. 10.14.0.2/16 or 10.64.x.y/16. Each key has its own. Empty means 10.14.0.2/16.
surfshark.addressFromConf: Taken from the config you pasted.

nordvpn.name: NordVPN
nordvpn.description: Paste an access token from your Nord Account, or your NordLynx private key.
nordvpn.credentialLabel: Access token or NordLynx private key

guide.title: How to get an access token
guide.step2: Choose NordVPN in the menu on the left.
guide.step3: Scroll down to Advanced settings → Set up NordVPN manually (Nord emails you a verification code).
guide.step4: On the Access token tab: Generate new token → choose how long it lasts → Copy, and paste it here.
guide.noteStored: The token is used once to fetch your NordLynx key and is not kept; you can delete it in your Nord Account after adding.
guide.noteService: The username and password under “Service credentials” are for OpenVPN — Proxy Farm doesn't use them.
guide.noteKey: Already have your NordLynx private key? You can paste the key instead.

expressvpn.name: ExpressVPN
expressvpn.description: Sign in with the username and password from your ExpressVPN account's Manual configuration (OpenVPN) page.

guide.title: How to get the username and password
guide.step1: Sign in at https://www.expressvpn.com/setup (your ExpressVPN account page).
guide.step2: Choose Manual configuration (under Set up devices / Advanced setup).
guide.step4: Copy the Username and Password from section 1 and paste them here. They are not your sign-in email and password, and not the activation code.
guide.noteActivation: An activation code alone isn't enough: you need to sign in to the website with the account's email.
guide.noteOvpn: You can also download a .ovpn file from section 2 and import it under Config file.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.collectsNothing: Proxy Farm collects nothing about you. There is no telemetry, no analytics and no crash reporting, and there is no Proxy Farm server.
privacy.local: Your accounts, ports and settings stay on this computer. Passwords, keys and tokens are encrypted by your operating system (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows).
privacy.providers: Each port connects to your VPN provider's servers with your own account. Surfshark ports also download Surfshark's public server list from api.surfshark.com, and Surfshark server names are looked up through Google Public DNS (dns.google) as well as your normal DNS. NordVPN ports download NordVPN's public server list from api.nordvpn.com, without your account; adding a NordVPN access token sends it once to api.nordvpn.com to fetch your NordLynx key, and the token is not kept. ExpressVPN ports look up ExpressVPN server names (expressnetw.com) through Google Public DNS (dns.google) as well as your normal DNS; there is no other ExpressVPN request besides the VPN connection itself. These requests come from your own IP address.
privacy.ipCheck: To confirm a tunnel works, Proxy Farm checks its exit IP and reachability through that tunnel, with api.ipify.org, ifconfig.co, ipinfo.io and www.gstatic.com. They see the tunnel's exit IP, not yours.
privacy.optional: The speed test (only when you run it) downloads a test file from speed.cloudflare.com through the port. The update check asks GitHub for the latest release, on start and once a day; you can turn it off under Updates.
privacy.delete: To delete all data: remove your accounts and ports, quit Proxy Farm, then delete its data folder: ~/Library/Application Support/Proxy Farm on macOS, %APPDATA%\Proxy Farm on Windows.
